source_allocation_constraints.scope: Internal exact arithmetic joins independently established source rates, eligible taxes and deduction bases to aggregate reconciliation. It is not a determination of statutory allocation priority, current-year policy or eligibility.
source_allocation_constraints.finding: When aggregate credit C is below the sum of independent source ceilings, feasible source allocations can be nonunique. Source i must lie between max(0,C-sum(other ceilings)) and min(C,ceiling_i). A correct annual total alone does not prove correct source deductions.
source_allocation_constraints.behavior: Derive unique allocations automatically, including one eligible source, nonbinding aggregate cap and zero total credit. Otherwise return allocation_required with exact source intervals and no invented source ledger. Explicit allocations must cover every source, sum exactly to reconciled credit and satisfy all source intervals; deductions and bases are recomputed per source.

aggregate_cap_arithmetic.contract: Internal exact-Fraction primitive for an independently established marginal schedule, fixed reduction and source-credit ceiling. Maximizes C subject to 0<=C<=source ceiling and C<=max(0,T(I-F+C)-reduction), with deduction F-C. Does not derive legal rates, eligibility, source allocation, rounding or refunds.
aggregate_cap_arithmetic.algorithm: Piecewise affine root calculation, including movement across marginal-band boundaries after deduction. Marginal rates strictly below1 make tax minus credit decreasing. No iterative decimal rounding or final-tax clamping substitutes for recalculating deductions.
aggregate_cap_arithmetic.counterexample_resolution: Under the explicitly conditional assumptions in the diagnostic, flat-rate total credit becomes2040000/167 and excess deduction1300000/167. Two-tier credit becomes48300000/367; the reconciled base falls below2million. All three conditional cases reconcile to zero tax after credit, and equal source splitting preserves aggregate results.

findings: Taxable FSIE receipts of a Hong Kong resident MNE may receive same-income credit capped by paid similar foreign tax and Hong Kong tax on that income.
CDTA tax claims and non-CDTA unilateral claims follow distinct routes. Ineligible bilateral direct tax is not automatically unilateral tax.
Dividend underlying profits tax not allowed bilaterally can qualify unilaterally when the MNE holds at least10percent equity at distribution. Never count the same underlying tax in both claims.
Exempt income receives no FSIE credit. A nonresident MNE may have an expense deduction route, which this credit component does not implement.
